title: OpenAI-compatible API
subtitle: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint is the common shape my local models, the voice engine and ActiveKV present to callers.

stats.label: tokens of model context the voice requests outgrew before the fix

lede: In Agent Swarm agents use models from my own GPUs and from hosted providers, and I did not want provider-specific code anywhere in the agent loop. I standardised every model on the OpenAI-compatible chat and tool-calling interface, so routing, budgets and tool checks are written once. Local open-weight models served by vLLM already speak it. For hosted providers that do not, I built small bridge services that translate their APIs into the same shape, rate-limit in Redis, and register and deregister themselves, so the agent loop never learns a vendor's API. With one interface, the router picks an endpoint by policy and load. Tools go out as function definitions in the standard request.
quote: I use a common interface as an architectural boundary.
evidence: Multi-provider LLM integration: local and hosted models standardised on the OpenAI-compatible chat and tool-calling interface, with bridge services translating providers and a router choosing by policy and load.
Tool-calling validation: every returned tool call checked against its JSON Schema in strict mode before it runs, so a malformed call from a local model fails as an error.
Real-time voice AI latency: a voice engine streaming clause by clause from an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with a tool-selection step removed after a catalog overflowed a 32,768-token context.
author: Corey James
